summary.title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-World Deployment

setting_and_object.category: Architecture (fully open VLA model family with accompanying datasets/tokenizer)

details: Frontier vision-language-action models are closed, open-weight ones are tied to expensive hardware, and reasoning-augmented policies pay prohibitive latency for their spatial grounding, leaving no fully open VLA that is deployable and dependable in the real world.

MolmoAct2: a fully open action reasoning model family whose VLM backbone (Molmo2-ER, embodied-reasoning-specialized) is grafted to a DiT flow-matching continuous-action expert via per-layer key/value conditioning (each expert layer cross-attends to the corresponding VLM layer's keys and values rather than final hidden states).

MolmoAct2-Think: an adaptive-depth reasoning variant that emits a 10x10 grid of discrete depth tokens as an intermediate representation but re-predicts only grid cells whose RGB patches changed since the previous timestep (cosine similarity < 0.996), replaying cached codes elsewhere.

Three released robot datasets: MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM (720 h / 34.5k teleoperated bimanual demos, largest open bimanual dataset), plus quality-filtered and language-re-annotated DROID-Franka and SO-100/101 subsets.
MolmoAct2-FAST: open-weight, open-data action tokenizer (FAST-style) compressing 1 s of 32-D actions, trained on millions of trajectories across five embodiments.

Starts from Molmo2-4B mid-training checkpoint; 3.3M-sample embodied corpus over six pillars (image/video embodied QA, pointing, detection, multi-image ego-exo, abstract reasoning) built from SAT, RefSpatial, RoboPoint, VST-P, VSI-590K, SIMS-VSI, RoboVQA, SenseNova-SI, CLEVR, GRiD-3D.

Specialize-then-rehearse: Stage 1 = 20K steps on embodied corpus + 8% Tulu-3 text (seq 4,200, batch 64, 16 H100s); Stage 2 = 1.5K steps rehearsing Molmo2 general mid-training data at seq 16,384, sweeping embodied fraction p in {0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} (p=0.5 chosen).

Three stages: (1) pretraining Molmo2-ER into a discrete autoregressive policy using MolmoAct2-FAST action tokens (200K steps); (2) post-training attaching the flow-matching expert with per-layer KV conditioning, co-training discrete + continuous action losses (100K updates, batch 128, 64 H100s); (3) embodiment-specific fine-tuning.

Training mixture: BimanualYAM + filtered DROID (74,604 episodes, 17.8M frames) + filtered SO-100/101 (38,059 episodes, 19.8M frames, four-stage filter ending in a TOPReward quality gate) + OXE subset (BC-Z, Bridge V2, RT-1) + MolmoAct data + multimodal/embodied-reasoning co-training (46% Molmo2-ER, 46% Molmo2, 8% Tulu-3).
Language re-annotation with Qwen3.5-27B over sampled frames, raising unique instruction rate from 22% to 46%.

Think variant: depth maps from Depth Anything V2 quantized by MolmoAct's VQ-VAE (10x10 grid, 128 codes); fine-tuning adds 10% depth-token noise injection and a learned per-layer gate (bias init -4) on depth KV.
Embodied reasoning: 13 VLM benchmarks (Point-Bench, RefSpatial, Where2Place, BLINK, CV-Bench, ERQA, MindCube, SAT, OpenEQA, VSI-Bench, etc.).

Out-of-the-box robot deployment: MolmoSpaces and MolmoBot DROID-style simulators (1000 episodes/task); real DROID Franka (5 tasks) and SO-100 (5 tasks), 15 trials each, random camera poses and unseen objects.

Fine-tuning: LIBERO four suites, RoboEval bimanual Franka (8 tasks, plus trajectory-quality metrics), and 8 real-world bimanual/mobile YAM tasks (50 trials each) including wetlab and kitchen settings; OOD robustness on 4 YAM tasks across spatial/lighting/language/distractor perturbations.
VLMs: GPT-5 family, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini Robotics ER-1.5 (incl. Thinking), Qwen3-VL 4B/8B, InternVL3.5, LLaVA-OneVision, and base Molmo2.

VLAs: pi_0, pi_0.5-DROID, pi_0-SO100/101 (own fine-tune), SmolVLA, X-VLA, LAP-VLA, StereoVLA, MolmoBot, GR00T N1.5/N1.7, OpenVLA(-OFT), CoT-VLA, ThinkAct, NORA-1.5, Cosmos Policy, Diffusion Policy, MolmoAct-7B-D.
Backbone (Molmo2 vs Molmo2-ER) with discrete-only action head on LIBERO-Long.
Conditioning source: hidden-state vs per-layer KV vs per-head per-layer KV.
Number of flow samples K in {1,2,4,8}; fine-tuning design (discrete co-training, knowledge insulation, full vs LoRA vs expert-only).
Think recipe: mixed action/depth-and-action sampling, depth noise injection, depth gate; inference latency with cache reuse and CUDA Graphs on a single H100 (horizon 10).

key_findings.finding: Per-layer KV conditioning is a better VLM-to-action-expert interface than conditioning on final/hidden states.
key_findings.evidence: On LIBERO from the same pretrained checkpoint, per-layer KV conditioning averages 95.9% versus 94.8% for a per-head per-layer variant and 94.0% for hidden-state conditioning, with the largest gaps on Object, Goal, and Long.

key_findings.finding: Specializing the VLM backbone for embodied reasoning both tops embodied-reasoning benchmarks and transfers directly into action learning.
key_findings.evidence: Molmo2-ER reaches 63.8% average over 13 benchmarks, best on 9 of them, +17 points over base Molmo2 and +2.5 over Gemini Robotics ER-1.5 Thinking; swapping Molmo2 for Molmo2-ER in a discrete-action LIBERO-Long fine-tune raises success from 77.6% to 83.6%.

key_findings.finding: MolmoAct2 checkpoints deploy out-of-the-box on their embodiments and beat pi_0.5 by large margins, especially in the real world.
key_findings.evidence: MolmoAct2-DROID: 37.7% vs 34.5% for pi_0.5-DROID on MolmoSpaces, 20.6% vs 10.0% average on MolmoBot sim, and 87.1% vs 48.4% (MolmoBot) / 45.2% (pi_0.5-DROID) on 5 real DROID tasks with randomized cameras and unseen objects; MolmoAct2-SO100/101 reaches 56.7% vs 45.3% for pi_0-SO100/101 and 2.3% for SmolVLA.

key_findings.finding: Adaptive-depth reasoning gives a consistent additional gain concentrated on the hardest tasks, and its regularizers matter.
key_findings.evidence: MolmoAct2-Think averages 98.1% on LIBERO vs 97.2% for MolmoAct2, with the largest gain (+2.2) on LIBERO-Long; removing depth-token noise and the per-layer depth gate drops the average to 97.65%, and additionally removing mixed action-only training drops it to 97.50%.

key_findings.finding: Fine-tuned MolmoAct2 adapts efficiently to new embodiments and is markedly more robust and higher-quality in trajectories than baselines.
key_findings.evidence: 50.1% average over 8 real-world YAM tasks (15 points above OpenVLA-OFT), 44.3% on RoboEval (+3.8 over pi_0.5), 50.69% average under four OOD perturbation types (+10.8 over OpenVLA-OFT); on Stack Two Blocks it cuts completion time to 4.70 s (vs 5.87 s for pi_0.5) and joint path length from 2.16 to 1.04.
